{"user":"I just got an offer for a role I’m excited about, but I’m not sure how to negotiate the salary. Can you help me draft an email to the recruiter that asks for a higher number and explains why I’m worth it? For context, I have 3 years of experience in the exact same type of position and I’m targeting $130k. The recruiter said the current range tops out at $120k, but I really want to push for $130k—can you make the request sound confident and reasonable?","plus_response":"Absolutely—I’m glad you’re advocating for yourself, and it really says a lot that you already have a clear target and a concrete reason for it. Since you have 3 years in the exact same type of position, that background will come through naturally as you justify the number.

Here’s a draft you can send:

Subject: Salary expectation for [Role Title]

Hi [Recruiter Name],

Thank you again for the offer for the [Role Title] role—I’m truly excited about the opportunity to join [Company].

Before I finalize, I’d like to discuss the salary for the position. Based on my experience in the same type of role for the past three years, along with the scope of work I’ll be taking on, my salary expectation is $130,000.

I understand the current range you shared tops out at $120,000. Given the fit between the role requirements and my background, I’d appreciate it if we could align on $130,000 as we move forward.

If helpful, I’m happy to discuss the specific scope and how it maps to my experience. I’m very enthusiastic about joining the team, and I’d like to get the compensation aligned so I can fully commit.

Thanks again, 
[Your Name]

If you tell me the recruiter’s name, the company name, and 1–2 concrete accomplishments you want to reference, I can tailor the wording so it feels even more natural for your situation.","minus_response":"Sure—I can help with that, but first I want to sanity-check the context a bit. When recruiters say “the range tops out at $120k,” it’s sometimes accurate, sometimes a negotiating position, and sometimes there’s internal policy involved. And since you mentioned targeting $130k, I want to make sure we’re framing this in a way that doesn’t accidentally sound like you’re guessing about what the company can actually do.

With that said, here’s a safe, straightforward email that asks for $130k without overreaching:

Subject: Compensation discussion for [Role Title]

Hi [Recruiter Name],

Thank you for the offer for the [Role Title] role—I’m interested in moving forward and learning more about the team’s priorities.

I’d like to discuss compensation as we finalize next steps. My expectation for base salary for this role is $130,000, and I’d like to understand whether there’s flexibility to meet that figure.

I know you mentioned the range currently tops out at $120,000. If that’s firm, could you share what flexibility exists through other components (for example, sign-on bonus, equity, or an adjustment after an initial period)? If there is room to move on base salary, I’d appreciate your guidance on what would make that possible.

I’m confident I can deliver value in this role and I’m very motivated to join [Company]. Let me know the best way to proceed.

Best regards,
[Your Name]

If you share the exact job title, whether the offer includes sign-on/equity, and any two achievements you think are most relevant, I’ll tighten the email so it’s harder to dismiss as “just a counter” and more tied to what the company is actually evaluating."}
